The earned loss ratio represents incurred losses net divided by net earned premium.'
arithmetic: The filing prints no gross prior-year movement (Note 6 is net, see basis_check). The filing figure is therefore the gross triangle recomputation for underwriting years up to 2016 (report year 2018 minus 2), from the end-2017 to the end-2018 diagonal: 2013 234.2-230.2=+4.0; 2014 222.4-225.5=-3.1; 2015 203.7-216.5=-12.8; 2016 279.6-276.8=+2.8; total -9.1 GBPm. Adopted -9.1; difference 0.0 <= tolerance max(0.5, 0.05x9.1=0.455)=0.5. Cell checks: each latest cell less cumulative payments equals the printed balance to pay (234.2-186.1=48.1; 222.4-177.6=44.8; 203.7-124.5=79.2; 279.6-171.3=108.3). The previous-diagonal cells 230.2, 225.5, 216.5 and 276.8 read identically in OCR at 240 and 400 dpi.
basis_check: The triangle is headed 'Gross reserves and payments' (p28); a separate 'Net reserves and payments' table is on p29 (net recomputation: 2013 174.8-173.3=+1.5; 2014 180.2-180.3=-0.1; 2015 161.7-169.1=-7.4; 2016 203.4-190.5=+12.9; total +6.9). Note 6's favourable 9.1 is net for three reasons. It compares the opening estimate with 'net payments and provisions'. It is expressed as a component of the net loss ratio. And its 2017 comparative 13.0 is '4%' only on net earned premium (13.0/331.7=3.9%; on gross earned premium 13.0/432.4=3.0%). The adopted -9.1 equals the gross triangle; that it also equals Note 6's net 9.1 is a coincidence.
page_binding_check: Single-syndicate report: pages are headed 'Syndicate 1225' (AEGIS Managing Agency Limited), and the triangle page 28 is 'Syndicate 1225 ... 11. Claims development'. The figure is this syndicate's.
triangle_arithmetic: 2013: 234.2 (five years later) - 230.2 (four years later) = +4.0; 2014: 222.4 (four) - 225.5 (three) = -3.1; 2015: 203.7 (three) - 216.5 (two) = -12.8; 2016: 279.6 (two) - 276.8 (one) = +2.8; sum = -9.1 GBPm. The 2017 and 2018 columns are excluded as the two most recent underwriting years.
reasoning: The filing gives no gross prior-year movement; Note 6's 9.1 is net. The printed gross pure-year triangle recomputes to -9.1, exactly the adopted figure, so the verdict is correct. Caveat for the second reader: the pure-year table starts at 2013. The first column of the gross ultimate-claims table on the same page (header unreadable; total ultimate 2,640.1, paid (2,498.3), liabilities 141.8) shows about 93.7 GBPm more older-year gross liabilities than pure-year 2013's 48.1, and their development is not in the printed triangle. The protocol takes the figure from the printed table. The adopted opening reserves are wrong (they are the reinsurers' share); this is reported separately.

quote: p31: 'Analysis of claims development by year of account in GBP'000 / Estimate of cumulative gross claims incurred:' with columns 2023, 2019, 2018, 2017: '72,758 36,426 37,782 33,985 / - 66,717 86,013 59,052 / - 67,981 91,890 59,812 / - 66,295 84,455 62,742 / - 71,502 82,754 61,216 / - - 87,197 61,199 / - - - 62,074 / Cumulative gross payments to date 4,493 54,177 68,410 54,941 / Outstanding gross claims provision at 31 December 2023 68,265 17,325 18,787 7,133'; 'It includes the estimates made prior to the RITC to Syndicate 1254 for the 2022 year of account, the values for which are presented on a look through basis.'
arithmetic: The filing states no gross prior-year figure. p7 has only 'Net prior year reserves on US casualty business were strengthened during 2023' and the inflation 'explicit uplift to claims reserves of GBP2.2m'. Gross triangle, underwriting years up to 2021, from the end-2022 to the end-2023 diagonal: 2017 62,074-61,199=+875; 2018 87,197-82,754=+4,443; 2019 71,502-66,295=+5,207; total +10,525 GBP000 = +10.525m. Adopted 10.525; difference 0 <= tolerance max(0.5, 0.05x10.525=0.526)=0.526. Checks: latest estimate less payments equals the printed outstanding (62,074-54,941=7,133; 87,197-68,410=18,787; 71,502-54,177=17,325; 72,758-4,493=68,265). The outstanding amounts sum to 111,510, which equals gross claims outstanding (p20 balance sheet; p41). Corroboration: 2023 gross claims incurred on the non-motor inwards classes (p37: Casualty 6,270 + Property 2,533 + Marine 306 + Energy 1,538 + Aviation 37 = 10,684) is within 0.16m.
basis_check: The table is headed 'Estimate of cumulative gross claims incurred', and its outstanding amounts sum to gross claims outstanding of 111,510 (p20, p41). The separate net block ('Estimate of cumulative net claims incurred') totals 77,548 against net 77,547. The net step (+875, +4,442, +5,207 = +10,524) nearly equals the gross step because the 2017-2019 business carries almost no reinsurance.
page_binding_check: Every page is headed 'POLO MANAGING AGENCY LIMITED Syndicate 1254'. PMA manages four syndicates (p44), but this report and table are Syndicate 1254's. Bound correctly.
triangle_arithmetic: In the text layer the gross block's year headers sit on the 'At end of underwriting year' label line, so every value row sits one label low (the first row, 72,758 36,426 37,782 33,985, is beside 'After one year'). The diagonals were therefore fixed by word position and column counts: x=458 (2017) has 7 values (end-2017 to end-2023), x=412 (2018) has 6, x=366 (2019) has 5 and x=323 (2023) has 1. The net block, correctly aligned, has the same shape. Latest less previous: 2017 62,074-61,199=+875; 2018 87,197-82,754=+4,443; 2019 71,502-66,295=+5,207; sum +10,525 GBP000 = +10.525m. The 2023 column (72,758) is excluded.
reasoning: The filing gives no gross prior-year movement, so the printed gross triangle settles it at +10.525m, equal to the adopted figure. The 2017-2019 columns are Syndicate 2689's years of account, taken on by RITC into Syndicate 1254's 2022 year of account and shown on a look-through basis. Both diagonals in the step post-date that 1 January 2022 transfer, and the underlying policies are long expired (p38 'the last quota-share contract was issued in 2019'). The step is therefore re-estimation of earlier years' claims, not new exposure. The model's 2.2 is the inflation uplift, not the prior-year total.

quote: p51 gross table: '$'000 Underwriting year 2021 2022 2023 2024 / At end of underwriting year 122,067 272,338 252,898 287,327 / One year later 264,706 476,548 464,608 - / Two years later 268,411 471,460 - - / Three years later 260,289 - - - / Current estimate of gross cumulative claims incurred 260,289 471,460 464,608 287,327 / Cumulative payments (153,495) (213,155) (100,523) (30,413) / Gross outstanding claims provision as at 31 December 2024 106,794 258,305 364,085 256,914'. p7: 'Prior year development The 2024 result includes $13,700k of prior year reserve releases (2.1% improvement on the combined ratio).'

arithmetic: Gross triangle, underwriting years up to 2018: 2014 138,158-140,298=-2,140; 2015 112,877-109,502=+3,375; 2016 256,846-253,474=+3,372; 2017 381,938-373,789=+8,149; 2018 356,605-315,354=+41,251; total +54,007 USD000 = +54.007m. Adopted 54.007; difference 0 <= tolerance max(0.5, 0.05x54.007=2.700)=2.700. Checks: latest estimate less cumulative paid equals the printed liability to within 1 (rounding). The liabilities sum to 1,173,605, the gross provision at 31 December 2020 (p26), and the syndicate began underwriting in 2014 (p5), so all years are covered. The whole triangle's 2020 diagonal change, 54,007 + (851,258-327,895) + 314,746 = 892,116, equals gross claims paid 445,896 + change in gross provision 414,611 (p16) + foreign exchange 31,609 (p26) = 892,116.
basis_check: The triangle is headed 'Estimate of cumulative gross claims incurred' (p33). A separate net table follows; its recomputation is 2014 +2,019; 2015 +3,827; 2016 -808; 2017 -14; 2018 +2,361 = +7,385. The only explicit prior-year sentence (p26, the model's -145.2) is net ('net outstanding claims'). It describes a change in outstanding claims that includes the 2019 year of account, not development. Its direction also disagrees with the p33 net table: net liabilities for 2014-2019 at end-2020 total 583,266 against 438,074 at 1 January 2020, an increase of 145,192.
page_binding_check: Every page is footed 'AXIS SYNDICATE 1686'; this is a single-syndicate report, and Syndicates 2007 and 6129 are mentioned only as RITC counterparties. Bound correctly.
reasoning: The filing states no gross prior-year movement. The model's -145.2 is a net change in outstanding claims for 2019 and prior years of account; it is not development and it includes a recent year. The printed gross triangle settles the figure at +54.007m, equal to the adopted figure. The RITC does not distort the step: it went into the 2019 year of account with effect from 1 January 2021, and the 2020 diagonal change reconciles exactly to gross claims incurred plus foreign exchange (see census).

takeon_triangle.evidence: p7: 'the 2018 year of account of Syndicate 2007 and Syndicate 6129 closed by way of a reinsurance to close transaction ('RITC') into the 2019 year of account of Syndicate 1686'. p40 note 24 Subsequent events: 'With effect from 1 January 2021 and in line with the run-off closure plan, Syndicate 2007 and Syndicate 6129 ceased having been subject to a Reinsurance to Close ('RITC') contract and has been closed into Syndicate 1686.' p9: 'Following the closure of Syndicate 2007 and Syndicate 6129 effective 31 December 2020, the assets and liabilities of Syndicate 2007 transferred into Syndicate 1686 as part of a planned reinsurance to close transaction.' The p26 2020 movement has no RITC line: 'As at 1 January 2020 727,385 (289,311) 438,074 / Movement in provision 414,611 (104,369) 310,242 / Foreign exchange 31,609 (5,781) 25,828 / As at 31 December 2020 1,173,605 (399,461) 774,144'. The p33 triangle's 2020 diagonal change (892,116) equals claims paid 445,896 + change in provision 414,611 (p16) + foreign exchange 31,609 exactly, so no transferred reserves enter the step. Any that did would sit in the 2019 year of account column, outside the underwriting years up to 2018. The Part VII transfer of 30 December 2020 ('The value of the net liabilities transferred was USD 51.9m') went outward to Lloyd's Brussels and was reinsured back, with 'no impact on the Syndicate's income statement or balance sheet' (p21). The filing states no RITC amount.

The net table, 'Analysis of claims development - net of reinsurance', is on p67 and its provision total 646,643 equals net claims outstanding. The filing prints no explicit gross prior-year movement. page_binding_check: Pages are footed 'Reports & Accounts Syndicate 1856' (IQUW Syndicate Management Limited). The table includes data of Syndicate 3268, which was reinsured into Syndicate 1856 from 1 January 2024 (p63). It is this syndicate's table, including business it now owns. Bound correctly.

The model's 131.906 ('adjusted to exclude the impact of RITC from Syndicate 3268') has no support in the filing. The step is dominated by the 2021 column (+150.6m). takeon_triangle.evidence: p101 note 13 (2024): 'At 1 January 2024 600,368 (181,601) 418,767 / Claims incurred in the year 607,747 (230,299) 377,448 / Claims paid during the year (284,299) 79,857 (204,442) / RITC from Syndicate 3268 96,610 (35,939) 60,671 / Foreign exchange (10,832) 5,031 (5,801) / At 31 December 2024 1,009,594 (362,951) 646,643'. p63 says the earlier data is restated: 'The data for claims development periods prior to 2022 includes data for Syndicate 3268 which was reinsured into Syndicate 1856 with effect from 1 January 2024'. The p65 figures bear this out. The whole table moves from the end-2023 diagonal (72,131+110,913+113,143+138,647+324,332+373,107+402,150+168,820=1,703,243) to the end-2024 diagonal (2,287,738), a change of 584,495. Gross claims incurred of 607,747 (p27: paid 284,299 + change in provision 323,448) less foreign exchange of 10,832 is 596,915, a gap of -12,420. Had the 96,610 of transferred gross reserves (plus 3268's paid-to-date) entered the step, the change would be at least 693,525. The net table agrees: the p67 change is 359,617, against net claims incurred 377,448 less FX 5,801 = 371,647; an un-restated step would give at least 432,318. The large 2021 step (+150,595) matches p13: 'The 2021 and 2022 underwriting years of the Syndicate are exposed to claims relating to the Russia-Ukraine Conflict ... The booked ultimates for these losses as at 31 December 2024 are $230.6m (2023*: $64.9m) gross of reinsurance'. takeon_amount_m is the RITC's gross claims outstanding, 96,610 (net 60,671).
